relevance.rationale: WRONG JOIN - report loudly. The seeded id was freedman2003, i.e. Freedman-Kitaev-Larsen-Wang, 'Topological Quantum Computation', arXiv:quant-ph/0101025. This document is arXiv:1012.5432v4 [quant-ph], 'Towards Topological Quantum Computation? Knotting and Fusing Flux Tubes', single author M. B. Thompson, dated 26 Dec 2012. Different paper, different author, different decade; the machine guess evidently keyed on the shared phrase 'Topological Quantum Computation'. The genuine freedman2003 PDF is a separate upload (uploads/freedman2003.pdf, quant-ph/0101025v2), triaged separately in this slice, so this row must not inherit that key. No registered key matches this document: grep of folio/schema/references.ts for '1012.5432' and for 'Thompson' returns only the unrelated Bilson-Thompson entries. Set id to null. Verdict undetermined rather than tangential because the identification is settled but the relevance question was never actually posed for THIS paper - it inherited a verdict earned by a different document, and I have read only its title page here. FIRST-PASS TRIAGE 2026-11-22 (bean qou-n6ge, agent assessment from the abstract and pp. 1-2): the paper computes particle content, spins and fusion rules of the Drinfeld quantum double D(H) for finite residual gauge groups H (S3, A5, and in appendices S4, A4, D4) with a MAGMA program. The braid-group/Yang-Baxter material is standard background. The folio uses no quantum double anywhere (grep of folio/ for 'quantum double' and D(A5) returns nothing), so the paper supplies no result a block relies on. Verdict tangential; the A5 fusion tables would become relevant only if a block took up D(A5) anyons.
